sections.vendors: Primark confirmed a multi-year recycled fibre partnership with Circ, which uses textile-to-textile recycling technology to process blended cotton-polyester garments into reusable fibres. The Circ facility (built with $500M investment) is targeting commercial-scale recycled polyester supply to Primark from 2029 onwards.
sections.sustainability: Primark reported 74% of fibres sourced from more sustainable routes as part of Primark Cares targets. The brand is actively reviewing its Primark Cares sustainability strategy in response to incoming EU textile regulations, particularly around extended producer responsibility (EPR) and digital product passports.
sections.sourcing: Bangladesh and India remain Primark's primary sourcing hubs. The brand is evaluating nearshoring options in response to geopolitical pressures on Asian supply chains, though no formal shift has been announced. Primark Cares mandates all Tier 1 suppliers undergo annual social audits.
sections.strategy: Primark continues its selective store expansion across the US and continental Europe. The brand is investing in digital tools for supply chain transparency while maintaining its no-online-sales model to keep prices low. New store formats with integrated 'Primark Cares' sustainability messaging are being rolled out.
sections.pricing: Primark remains committed to its value positioning, with no major price increases signalled despite cost pressures from energy, logistics and sustainable material premiums. The brand's scale (ABF group buying power) gives it leverage to absorb sustainable fibre cost premiums.
sections.launches: Primark launched several licensed collaborations for Autumn/Winter 2026, including character-based ranges and an expanded athletic-leisure line. The school uniform range saw elevated sustainable materials content with BCI cotton and recycled polyester blends.
sections.gossip: Trade press commentary suggests Primark is under pressure to accelerate its digital product passport rollout ahead of EU mandates. Some sourcing analysts note Primark's recycled polyester 2029 target from the Circ partnership may be optimistic given scale-up challenges in textile recycling.
soWhat: The Circ partnership signals long-term demand for recycled polyester at scale — suppliers investing in GRS-certified recycled polyester production are well positioned for Primark contracts from 2028-29
74% sustainable fibre sourcing target creates near-term procurement pressure — suppliers without BCI, GRS, GOTS, or OEKO-TEX certification risk delisting from Primark's Tier 1 approved list
No nearshoring movement yet, but EU EPR regulations monitoring is creating pressure — Bangladesh and India vendors should prepare digital traceability documentation and scope 3 reporting capability
